intro: Advice with distance, warnings, threats and promises: how to say "be careful" in Spanish.
p.advertir.consejo: The e becomes «ie»: «advierto», «adviertes». You say «te advierto que…» and an indicative follows.
p.ojo.consejo: It is a short warning: «¡ojo con el escalón!». It is the word for the organ of sight, but here it means «careful».
p.fiarse de.consejo: It takes «de»: «no te fíes de él». «Fíes» has an accent to keep the i and the e apart.
p.prestar atención a.consejo: You say «prestar», not «pagar»: «presta atención a la letra pequeña». «A» comes after.
p.si yo fuera tú.consejo: A conditional follows: «si yo fuera tú, no firmaría». Here «fuera» is from «ser».
p.lo mejor sería que.glosa: the best thing would be for…
p.lo mejor sería que.consejo: It takes the imperfect subjunctive: «lo mejor sería que preguntaras». It is soft advice.
p.te recomendaría que.consejo: It takes the imperfect subjunctive: «te recomendaría que leyeras». Synonym: «te aconsejaría que…».
p.amenaza.consejo: It is feminine: «una amenaza». The verb is «amenazar», with z. The z sounds like th.
p.asegurar.consejo: You say «te aseguro que…» and the next verb is indicative: «te aseguro que es verdad».
p.jurar.consejo: The j sounds like h: hu-RAR. «Te lo juro» is a very strong promise between friends.
p.arrepentirse de.consejo: The e becomes «ie»: «me arrepiento». It takes «de»: «me arrepiento de no ir».
p.como no.consejo: With the subjunctive it is a threat or a warning: «como no vengas, me enfado». With the indicative it means «since not».
p.letra pequeña.consejo: It refers to the conditions of a contract. It is written as two words: «letra pequeña».
p.estafar.consejo: This verb gives «la estafa» and «el estafador». A price that is too low can be a sign.
b1.texto:
**Advice with distance.** You put yourself in the other person's place:

- **Si yo fuera tú**, no firmaría.
- **Lo mejor sería que** lo **consultaras** con un abogado.
- **Te recomendaría que leyeras** el contrato.

**Warnings.**

- **Te advierto que** no es fácil.
- **¡Ojo con** ese vendedor!
- **No te fíes de** nadie.
- **Presta atención a** la letra pequeña.

**Threats.** A warning with a consequence:

- **Como no** me **pagues**, te denuncio.
- **Te vas a arrepentir.**

**Promises** stronger than «te lo prometo»:

- **Te aseguro que** es verdad.
- **Te juro que** no fui yo.
b2.titulo: A flat that is too cheap
b2.f0.texto: I have found a flat in the centre for three hundred euros.
b2.f2.texto: I only have to send the money before seeing it.
b2.f3.texto: If I were you, I would not send a single euro.
b2.f4.texto: The owner has assured me that he is trustworthy.
b2.f6.texto: And what do I do, then?
b2.f7.texto: The best thing would be for you to ask to see the flat.
b2.f8.texto: And if he does not show it to me?
b2.f9.texto: If he does not show it to you, forget it.
b4.texto:
Each intention asks for a different construction:

- **Si yo fuera tú** + conditional: **si yo fuera tú, no firmaría**.
- **Lo mejor sería que** and **te recomendaría que** + imperfect subjunctive.
- **No te fíes de…**: the negative command takes the present subjunctive.
- **Como no** + present subjunctive = threat: **como no pagues, te denuncio**.
- **Te advierto que** and **te aseguro que** + indicative.
- **Arrepentirse de**: the e becomes ie: **me arrepiento**.
b4.e0.texto: If I were you, I would not sign anything.
b4.e1.texto: If you do not pay, I will report you.
b4.e2.texto: I warn you that it is not easy.
b5.f0.texto: The table lamp lights up a contract full of tightly packed paragraphs.
b5.f1.texto: Sonia follows the lines with her finger and moves her lips without making a sound.
b5.f2.texto: The tiny letters dance a little before her tired eyes.
b5.f3.texto: On the last page, a small sentence hides under a signature.
b5.f4.texto: Sonia breathes deeply and underlines the sentence with a red pencil.
b5.f5.texto: Outside, the rain taps the glass with thin, quick fingers.
b5.f6.texto: Sonia lets the phone ring on the table.
b5.f7.texto: A message glows on the screen with sweet promises and urgent deadlines.
b5.f8.texto: Sonia reads it twice and feels a light chill on the back of her neck.
b5.f9.texto: At last she closes the folder and switches off the lamp, without regretting anything.
b6.frase: Lo mejor sería que ____ con ella.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after «sería» comes the imperfect subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is present; after a conditional comes the imperfect.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is conditional; after «que» you need the subjunctive.
b6.pregunta: Complete the advice with the right verb.
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is not an invitation to look, but a warning.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It gives no information: it warns of a danger.
b7.pregunta: What does «¡Ojo con el escalón!» mean?
b8.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «como no» with the subjunctive is a threat.
b8.o2.refuerzo: The future does not follow «como no» in a threat.
b8.pregunta: Complete the threat with the right verb.
b9.frase: Si yo fuera tú no firmaría nada
b9.traduccion: If I were you, I would not sign anything
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «jurar» is promising with great force.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It only promises to try, not to do it.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Do not trust him.»
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «arrepentirse» is feeling sorry for what you did.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is not about time, but about regret.
b12.pregunta: What does «Te vas a arrepentir» mean?
p.encontrado.consejo: With «he», it forms the perfect: «he encontrado», I have found.
p.mandar.consejo: «mandar» also means to order. Context shows the meaning.
p.mandaría.consejo: The -ría ending is the conditional, used for «if I were you».
p.asegurado.consejo: From «asegurar», to guarantee. Its root is «seguro», safe.
p.fíes.consejo: «no te fíes» is a warning: do not trust.
p.pidieras.consejo: «pedir» changes e to i. The subjunctive here is past.
p.enseñe.consejo: «enseñar» means to show or to teach. The ñ sounds like «ny».
p.olvídate.consejo: The pronoun «te» attaches to the imperative. The v sounds like b.
p.firmaría.consejo: Conditional of «firmar», used with «si yo fuera tú».
p.pagues.consejo: After «como» with a condition, the subjunctive appears.
p.denuncio.consejo: From «denunciar», to report a crime to the authorities.
p.advierto.consejo: The v sounds like b. «advertir» means to warn.
p.párrafos.consejo: Each block of text in a document is a «párrafo».
p.apretados.consejo: From «apretar», to press together. Here it describes tight lines.
p.labios.consejo: The lips move when we speak. Plural of «labio».
p.diminutas.consejo: Very small. The feminine plural agrees with «letras».
p.ante.consejo: Also used for «ante» meaning in front of someone, in formal style.
p.subraya.consejo: From «raya», a line. To underline is to draw a line under a word.
p.finos.consejo: Its opposite is «gruesos», thick. It agrees with «dedos».
p.rápidos.consejo: Its opposite is «lentos», slow. It agrees with «dedos».
p.dulces.consejo: Also means candy. Here it describes pleasant words.
p.plazos.consejo: A set time limit for doing something. From «plazo».
p.urgentes.consejo: The g before e sounds like h. Plural of «urgente».
p.nuca.consejo: The back part of your neck, just under your head.
p.hablaras.consejo: The h is silent. «hablar» means to speak.
p.escalón.consejo: A single step of a staircase. From «escalera», stairs.
p.sales.consejo: «salir» means to go out. The form ends in -es for tú.
p.estudies.consejo: Subjunctive after «como no» to set a condition.
p.juro.consejo: The j sounds like h. «Te lo juro» means I swear to you.
